newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Oak sees return to profit in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Royal Oak sees return to profit in 1999.

text.p: Gold and copper miner Royal Oak Mines Ltd said on Monday it expected to break even next year and return to profit in 1999.

"We're basically looking at a break-even scenario for all of 1998 and then returning to profitability in the year 1999 and moving forward from there," Royal Oak chief financial officer James Wood said in a conference call with analysts on Monday.
Royal Oak, based in Kirkland, Washington, reported a C$60.2 million loss in the six months ended June 30, compared to a C$5.1 million profit in the first half of 1996.
The company said the forecast is based on an expected average gold price of US$343 an ounce in 1998, copper prices of around US$1 per pound, and a Canadian dollar worth about US$0.72.
Royal Oak has recently taken several steps to conserve cash in the face of weak gold prices, including delaying projects and closing two mines.
Royal Oak is among several Canadian gold miners that have seen profits slump due to sustained weakness in gold prices.
"Looking at gold over the last six to eight months, it's been a dreadful experience I think for all of us," said Royal Oak Chief Executive Margaret Witte.
Witte said Royal Oak's hedging program for the rest of 1997 was at US$395 an ounce. "The company has no gold hedged for next year," Witte said.

If gold prices do not recover to the US$340 an ounce level within the next few weeks, Witte said Royal Oak would put in place a strategy to ensure "that we are delivering into gold contracts next year that are above the spot price of gold."
Meanwhile, Royal Oak said it expected mining and milling operations at its Hope Brook Mine in Newfoundland to close down at the end of this week. Assets worth C$8 million at Hope Brook will be sold.
Mining at the Colomac mine in the Northwest Territories will stop at the end of August. Milling was expected to continue until October, said Chief Operating Officer Ed Szol.
Royal Oak took a C$39.7 million writedown on Colomac in the latest second quarter. It also took C$37.6 million in writedowns on the Hope Brook and Colomac mines in the fourth quarter of 1996.
"We've definitely put the worst behind us with Colomac and Hope Brook, and Kemess is going to be our very bright future," Witte told analysts.

The C$425 million Kemess gold and copper project in British Columbia was on schedule to start up in April 1998, Witte said. She added the project was fully funded and rejected market speculation that the company may not have the funding to complete the project.

The financing for Kemess includes cash and securities of C$190 million; C$89 million in permitted debt capacity; compensation and assistance from the provincial government worth up to C$166 million; and cash from current operations.
"We do have enough cash to complete and we're putting all of our other projects on hold and conserving cash to ensure we get started satisfactorily in April of next year," Witte said.
Royal Oak stock fell 0.04 to 2.52 on turnover of 231,700 shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday.
